question: What is the meaning of modular construction including geometry in relation to prefabrication?
description: Modular construction refers to the process of building prefabricated sections or modules that are later assembled on-site to form a complete structure. This approach allows for the prefabrication of components, which can be manufactured in a controlled factory environment, leading to increased efficiency, reduced construction time, and potentially lower costs. The geometry in relation to prefabrication refers to the design and layout of these prefabricated modules, which are created with precise dimensions and connections to ensure they fit together seamlessly when assembled on-site. This modular approach enables flexibility in design and construction, as well as the potential for easier future modifications or expansions.

stage of the building, it needs to be questioned if the existence of the MP 
in the pre-demolition phase has any value and if it helps to optimize the 
end-of-life phase of a material or element. It is obvious, that in the pre- 
demolition phase the state-of-the-art waste streams cannot be changed 
easily, due to the restricted time, which is why the MP should already be 
existing before the demolition-decision of a building. The existence of an 
MP in earlier stages, might enable the planning of the final stage of an 
element or material, thus might enable higher reuse or recycling rates. 
However, invasive methods, as applied within the UMA, can only be 
utilized, if the building is a demolition object. Therefore, in order to 
obtain the material and geometry information of a building prior- 
demolition, non-invasive methods are required. 
6. Conclusion 
In this paper, the application of the MP-method at the end-of-life 
phase was demonstrated on a real building, a lab and office facility of 
TU Wien. Since for the compilation of an MP information on the exact 
material composition, as well as geometry of buildings is required, 
various data acquisition methods were applied. To figure out the exact 
geometry of the building, a surveying company applied laser scanning 
technology, upon which a point-cloud was generated, which served as 
basis for creating a BIM-model. For detecting the exact material 
composition, through the UMA, a detailed investigation in the building 
including knocking and drilling was conducted. In order to determine 
the value of the embedded materials regarding reuse and recycling po­
tential, the quality of the building elements, within the scope of a pre- 
demolition audit with consideration of the separability of materials 
was acquired. A BIM-model was generated upon the acquired material 
information as well as a point cloud based on laser scanning. Finally, the 
MP-assessments were carried out through exporting a list with all rele­
vant information out of BIM and mapping the indicators from IBO to 
each material layer. 
The main outcomes of this paper can be summed up as follows:  
- A thorough acquisition of the geometry and material composition of 
buildings with regards to the quality and separability of materials 
was required to generate an MP  
- The MP assessed the total masses, recyclable and waste masses, the 
recycling potential as well as environmental impacts. Thus, it serves
